idea_name: Mean-variance portfolio covariance as multi-asset risk structure
mechanism: Estimate expected daily returns and full covariance of pct-change closes across a symbol set; solve max μ'w − ½ w'Σw with Σw=1, w≥0 (cvxpy/OLS-style). Optional SMA-gate adjusts returns by position so only in-signal bars enter Σ.
data_needed: Aligned D1 OHLC closes for each symbol; optional short/long MA windows for signal-gated returns
why_new_for_mis: Treats the live multi-asset covariance/expected-return vector itself as a cross-market risk-structure sensor usable for MIS exposure gating, not only as an optimizer black box.
quote: Such programs systematically analyze vast amounts of historical data market trends and asset correlations to determine optimal asset allocations that maximize potential returns while minimizing overall portfolio risk.

idea_name: FSCA factor-structure and unique-variation count as feature-regime sensor
mechanism: Standardize feature matrix X; EVD of correlation → principal components and cumulative % variance; Forward Selection Component Analysis greedily picks original columns maximizing explained variance (with optional SPBR backward refinement), yielding ordered FSVs/FSCs and a count k of unique variation sources (often ≪ v when features are redundant).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 100×9 demo run on BTCUSD D1 chart; general financial time-series features
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an interpretable count of independent variation sources and a factor-loading structure from correlated indicator packs—usable as a regime of feature redundancy vs. genuine multi-factor market structure.
quote: When we run the script and analyze the characteristics of the principal components, we find that there are only six unique sources of variation out of the nine.

idea_name: Cross-validated stepwise selection with MCP chance and spurious-improvement p-values
mechanism: Keep top-K candidate subsets each iteration; add features by CV criterion (1−SSE/n); Monte Carlo permute target to get (a) p(chance occurrence of current set) and (b) p(spurious improvement from last add); stop on degradation or max predictors. Model-agnostic via fitModel/evalModel hooks.
data_needed: Predictor matrix + target; num_folds, num_replications, min/max predictors
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 100×10 matrix demo on BTCUSD D1; linear-quadratic OLS example
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS with statistically gated feature-admission sensors (chance vs genuine lift) that work across arbitrary learner backends—useful before trusting any indicator→target link.
quote: Probability of chance occurrence: This probability measures the likelihood that the observed performance of the current feature set could be attributed to chance, assuming all selected features are irrelevant.

idea_name: Adaptive-partitioning mutual information and MRMR for nonlinear indicator relevance
mechanism: Estimate continuous MI via recursive 2×2/4×4 chi-square adaptive partitioning (Capm); MRMR selects argmax(I(Xi;Y) − avg I(Xi;Xj∈S)); solo and group MCP p-values on relevance/sum-relevance. Demo: MFI/MA/Bears/Bulls over lookbacks → next-bar log returns.
data_needed: Candidate indicator buffers + forward returns; chi_critical≈6; NumReplications
why_new_for_mis: Nonlinear, redundancy-aware relevance sensor for packing MIS feature panels—catches dependencies Pearson misses and down-weights collinear MA periods.
quote: Mutual information is a valuable tool for identifying effective predictors, especially when dealing with complex, nonlinear relationships.

idea_name: GRNN and variance-weighted ensembles as noise-robust consensus sensors
mechanism: Combine N pretrained numeric models via (i) simple average, (ii) unconstrained/constrained (biased/unbiased) linear weights, (iii) inverse-MSE variance weights, or (iv) GRNN interpolating component forecasts→target with annealed σ; demo shows GenReg best on clean data and averaging/weighting robust on noisy mixes.
data_needed: Array of IModel* forecasts on shared predictors; train targets for weight/GRNN fit
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic good/bad/biased FFNN models; demo script on BTCUSD D1 chart
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a deployable consensus layer that turns a bank of weak numeric sensors into a single noise-tolerant reading, with GRNN specifically for small/noisy regimes.
quote: GRNN excels in handling small, noisy datasets by effectively smoothing the data, though it may sacrifice some fitting power for larger, cleaner datasets.

idea_name: Local-accuracy and fuzzy-integral classifier ensembles for region-specialist regimes
mechanism: ClocalAcc: for an unknown case, pick the component classifier with highest accuracy among k-NN training neighbors that agreed on the same class (Woods et al.); CFuzzyInt: Sugeno λ-fuzzy measure of model reliabilities integrates class memberships. Also Borda/majority/union for ranked class-set reduction.
data_needed: Ensemble of IClassify models emitting class scores/ranks; training matrix for localAcc/fuzzy fit
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic multi-class MLP demos on BTCUSD D1; general classification tasks
why_new_for_mis: Turns specialist classifiers into a space-local regime router—MIS can sense which model’s territory the market is in, not just a global vote.
quote: When evaluating an unknown case, the system collects classifications from all component models and selects the model deemed most reliable for that specific case.

idea_name: Forward high-volatility binary classifier (75th-percentile spike warning)
mechanism: Label y=1 iff rolling std of returns over forward_window (default 12 H1 bars) exceeds the 75th percentile of that future-vol series; XGBClassifier on ATR/vol/vol_change, Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Rogers-Satchell, candle body/shadow ratios, and hour/day Fourier features; emit P(high-vol) and alert above threshold (default 0.7).
data_needed: OHLC + tick_volume from MT5; lookback_periods (5,10,20); forward_window; volatility_threshold percentile
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 (10k bars train); GUI also GBPUSD, USDJPY; forecast horizon ~12 hours
why_new_for_mis: Operational MIS volatility-regime change sensor: classifies impending extreme-vol clusters rather than regressing exact σ, with explicit probability suitable for stop-width / risk-mode switching.
quote: Instead of predicting specific values, we began to define two states: normal/low volatility (label 0) and high volatility above the 75th percentile (label 1).

idea_name: Multi-estimator vol feature pack with cyclic time encoding
mechanism: Build scaled feature vector from rolling std, ATR, Parkinson √(ln(H/L)²/(4ln2)), Garman-Klass, Rogers-Satchell, relative vol/ATR changes, body_ratio/upper/lower shadows, plus hour_sin/cos and day_sin/cos; target is future realized vol (regression) or high-vol class.
data_needed: OHLC bars; lookback set; StandardScaler fit on train window
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 primary; multi-TF discussion (tick to daily) for regime labels low/trend/explosive
why_new_for_mis: Concrete, stationarity-aware vol feature recipe MIS can reuse as inputs to any downstream regime model, including session-phase cyclic gates.
quote: volatility, unlike price, has the property of stationarity — it tends to return to its mean value and forms stable patterns.

idea_name: Live equity/balance drawdown and daily-weekly loss-limit state sensor
mechanism: AccountMonitor thread every ~18s computes balance and equity drawdown vs historical MAX from SQLite; aggregates today/week losing deals; flags when daily/weekly % or absolute loss or max_drawdown thresholds breach; optional auto-close + trade block.
data_needed: MT5 account_info, positions_get, history_deals_get; user risk_settings (daily/weekly limits, drawdown_mode)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any Forex account/symbols under MT5; continuous 24/7 monitoring
why_new_for_mis: Account-level risk-state sensor MIS can fuse with market sensors to gate sizing/mode when capital drawdown regime turns hostile.
quote: the system monitors both the drawdown on balance and equity, and can automatically close positions when a set threshold is reached

idea_name: SSA relative singular spectrum elbow for signal-vs-noise structure
mechanism: Build Hankel trajectory matrix (window L≈N/2); SVD; plot σi²/∑σj²; select eigentriples before the spectral elbow; group into trend/seasonal/noise; diagonal-average reconstruct; LRR from left singular vectors for multi-step forecast. Relative spectrum shape distinguishes periodic (paired equal σ), trend (one dominant), or pure noise (smooth decay).
data_needed: Univariate series length N; window L; rank r of kept components; forecast horizon
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic sinus+noise, trend+sinus+noise, random walk, white noise; Basic-SSA vs SingularSpectrumAnalysisForecast; aimed at financial prices
why_new_for_mis: Non-parametric structural sensor that separates deterministic cycles/trends from noise without stationarity assumptions—usable for MIS pattern confirmation and short-horizon structural forecasts.
quote: Typically, components are selected before the point of sharp decline (the so-called "elbow" on the graph).

idea_name: SSA-based change-point detection path for abrupt behavior shifts
mechanism: Article notes SSA extends to multidimensional data and can underpin a change-point indicator detecting sudden shifts in financial-instrument behavior by monitoring structural breaks in reconstructed components / spectrum.
data_needed: Price or multi-series trajectory matrices over rolling windows
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: General financial instruments; univariate SSA scripts as base
why_new_for_mis: Explicitly points MIS toward SSA-derived change-point sensing for regime breaks—complementary to spectral elbow structure sensing.
quote: It can be used to construct a change-point detection indicator to detect sudden changes in the behavior of financial instruments.

idea_name: HSIC kernel independence test as nonlinear feature–target dependence sensor
mechanism: Gaussian RBF kernels K,L with median-heuristic σ; empirical HSIC=coef·sum(Kc⊙L); significance via permutation (~1000 shuffles of L) or Gamma approximation of n·HSIC; reject independence if p<α. Works for scalar or vector X vs Y without modeling P(X,Y).
data_needed: Feature matrix X (n×d) and target Y; alpha; optional Bootstrap permutations
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic nonlinear Y=X1²·cos(π·X2)+noise; framed for trading feature selection on quotes
why_new_for_mis: Pre-model gate that senses whether MIS features actually share any (including nonlinear) dependence with the target—Pearson-blind relationships included.
quote: Unlike the correlation coefficient, which only identifies linear relationships, HSIC is capable of detecting both linear and non-linear relationships.

idea_name: Gaussian-process posterior uncertainty bands as predictive confidence sensor
mechanism: GP prior with sum of RBF+Linear+Periodic(+White) kernels; optimize hyperparameters by NLML (Cholesky+BLEIC); Predict returns μ* and Σf*/Σy* so ±2σ bands quantify latent-function vs observation uncertainty; RBF alone collapses to prior mean out-of-sample, linear/periodic enable extrapolation.
data_needed: Train (X,y) with optional noise; kernel_list; test X*
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS with calibrated predictive uncertainty—not just a point forecast—so regime confidence / extrapolation risk can be sensed from band width.
quote: This allows the model to provide not only point predictions but also uncertainty estimates, typically expressed as confidence intervals.

idea_name: DMD eigenvalue magnitude and growth-rate as oscillatory-mode stability sensor
mechanism: Time-delay embed univariate series into tall Hankel-like snapshots; DynamicModeDecomposition(X1,X2) → Ritz values λ; |λ|>1 growing/unstable, |λ|<1 decaying, |λ|≈1 stable oscillation; continuous growth_rate=Re(λ)/Δt and frequency=Im(log λ)/(2π Δt); amplitudes rank dominant modes for filtered reconstruction/short forecasts.
data_needed: Univariate series; Δt between snapshots; Delay embedding; SVD rank/tol
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic oscillatory demo; AUDUSD PERIOD_D1 close (StartDate 2025.06.02, 100 bars + forecasts)
why_new_for_mis: Turns price into a bank of spatiotemporal modes whose stability/growth rates are direct MIS regime features—growth modes flag unstable structure, near-unit-circle modes flag persistent cycles.
quote: Magnitude > 1: The mode is unstable and grows over time. Magnitude < 1: The mode is considered to be stable, even though there are signs of decay. Magnitude = 1: The mode is stable and oscillates without growth or decay.

idea_name: DMD residual norms and short-horizon filtered forecast quality
mechanism: Residual vector per mode = actual snapshot − DMD prediction; residual norms near 0 ⇒ faithful linear dynamics; filtered reconstruction zeros low-amplitude modes; forecasts by extending Vandermonde dynamics beyond last time—article shows price series only trustworthy for a few steps before breakdown under noise.
data_needed: Fitted CDmd model; optional mode mask; num_future_steps
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDUSD D1 closes; synthetic clean signal vs noisy price
why_new_for_mis: Residual-norm and forecast-horizon degradation give MIS a live fidelity meter for when linear modal structure still holds—i.e., a change sensor for model-breakdown / regime departure.
quote: Confirming that DMD is only really usefull for short-term forecasts. Anything more that a couple of steps into the future, and the model starts to breakdown.
